$comment: Model registry for the Bedrock proxy. This file is the allowlist: a model id absent
here is rejected with HTTP 400 before any credit reservation, because an unlisted model
would reach Bedrock with no token-accounting policy attached.
To add a model: append an entry and redeploy. Fields:
provider          vendor family (anthropic|openai|xai|google|nvidia|qwen)
bedrock_model_id  the id sent upstream (inference-profile id or foundation-model id)
bedrock_region    the region this model is invoked in
aliases           client-facing names that resolve to this entry; must be globally unique
wire_protocol     messages = Bedrock Converse, responses = bedrock-mantle OpenAI surface
pricing_key       row in the pricing table; a key is ONE price point, so models
at different published prices do not share one
price_model_id    the id the price APIs know this model by, when the billed
spelling differs from bedrock_model_id (optional)
served_by         bedrock (default) | vllm | semantic-router
endpoint_key      required when served_by=vllm (an allowlist token, never a URL)
virtual           true marks a pool placeholder that must never be a billed model
sr_pool_ref       names the semantic-router pool a virtual entry stands for
notes             why this entry looks the way it does; carried in the data on purpose
A Converse entry also needs bedrock:Converse on its model ARN in the task role
(iac/lib/ecs-stack.ts). Adding one here without that fails loudly at invoke time.
bedrock_region is asymmetric by design: it is AUTHORITATIVE for wire_protocol
"responses" (each mantle model is offered in specific regions), and ADVISORY for
"messages" — the Converse chain is built from the deployment's BEDROCK_REGION plus
STRATOCLAVE_FAILOVER_REGIONS, so a Converse model must be offered in those regions
or it should not be registered at all. That is why the Qwen entry is
qwen3-next-80b-a3b and not qwen3-235b-a22b-2507, which Bedrock offers only in us-west-2.

models.notes: Shares pricing_key "opus" with Opus 4.5 through 4.8, whose in-region rate is the same $5.50/$27.50 per MTok (measured 2026-08-31 against bedrock:ListFoundationModelAgreementOffers). Opus 4 and 4.1 are NOT in this tier — they list at $15/$75 — and carry "opus-legacy".

Priced above the Opus tier: $11/$55 per MTok in-region, $10/$50 global (measured 2026-08-31). It carries its own pricing_key rather than sharing "opus". The Bedrock offering requires the account to opt into provider_data_share and has a higher refusal rate than prior Claude models.

Priced at $15/$75 per MTok, three times the Opus 4.5+ rate, so it cannot share "opus": a key is charged at its dearest member, and sharing would charge every Opus 5 request at this rate. Measured 2026-08-31 from the Price List's AmazonBedrockFoundationModels offer.

Lists BELOW the Sonnet 4.x tier — $2.20/$11.00 per MTok in-region against $3.30/$16.50 — so it carries its own key. It shared "sonnet" until the live feed's key-spread check measured the difference (2026-08-31).
Priced at $3/$15 per MTok — the Sonnet 4.x tier's in-region rate is $3.30/$16.50, so this shares a key with Claude 3 Sonnet instead of with the current tier.
Priced at $0.80/$4.00 per MTok against Haiku 4.5's $1.10/$5.50, so it carries its own key. The Latency Optimized variant is a different product at $1.00/$5.00 and is not served here.
Priced at $0.25/$1.25 per MTok. Bedrock publishes no prompt-cache rate for it because it does not support prompt caching; the key's cache legs are therefore an upper bound, not a published price.

Flagship GPT-5.6 tier on bedrock-runtime OpenAI-compatible endpoint; its own pricing_key because each tier is a distinct model card with its own price. Region is PINNED to us-east-2 to reuse the region already proven by the earlier gpt-5.5 entry, even though the model is also offered elsewhere. Invoked through the `bedrock-runtime` OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is the one AWS recommends; `bedrock_model_id` carries the `us.` inference-profile prefix because that endpoint refuses the bare id with "Invocation ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported", and because every Anthropic entry already stores its profile id the same way.

Balanced GPT-5.6 tier on bedrock-runtime OpenAI-compatible endpoint; its own pricing_key for the same reason as sol. Region is PINNED to us-east-2 for the same reason as sol. Invoked through the `bedrock-runtime` OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is the one AWS recommends; `bedrock_model_id` carries the `us.` inference-profile prefix because that endpoint refuses the bare id with "Invocation ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported", and because every Anthropic entry already stores its profile id the same way.

Served on bedrock-runtime OpenAI-compatible endpoint's OpenAI-compatible surface, so it rides the same transport as the OpenAI family — no new transport, just an entry. Offered in us-west-2. Invoked through the `bedrock-runtime` OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is the one AWS recommends; `bedrock_model_id` carries the `us.` inference-profile prefix because that endpoint refuses the bare id with "Invocation ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported", and because every Anthropic entry already stores its profile id the same way.

Served by Converse, so it rides the same transport as the Claude family. Not Claude, so resolve_bedrock_model() keeps it out of /v1/messages; reachable only via /v1/chat/completions. Priced at $0.15/$0.65 per MTok in the Price List's AmazonBedrock offer (measured 2026-08-31); no prompt-cache rate is published, so the key's cache legs are an upper bound.

Chosen over qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 because Bedrock offers that one only in us-west-2, outside a us-east-1 residency policy. Converse transport; same /v1/messages exclusion and same unpriced-defaults-high rule as nemotron.
